guide.biology: Open water lets dissolved things and swimmers move freely, while many attached microbes need a surface to hold on to.
guide.rules: Turns covered cells into water without removing any life, deposits or dissolved fields. Dissolved things spread fastest in water: 0.10 per tick, against 0.025 in gel and 0.01 in sediment. Gas exchange with the air runs at full rate. Water offers no attachment surface of its own; stone edges and attachment mesh provide one. Organisms that cannot live in water respond through ordinary suitability. No additional modeled reaction.
guide.example: Paint a water channel through gel and watch sugar spread along it.
